* The stored `dueAt` is never touched. The NOTIFICATION kind used to snooze by rewriting

missed.fact: Snooze is device-local, not a ReminderEntity column and not synced. It lives in the Preferences DataStore as a long key 'pending_snooze:<reminderId>' holding the re-alert trigger time in epoch millis. The source says this is deliberate: a snooze pressed on one phone must not ring on another. A merge must not expect snooze in the reminder schema or the sync payload.

The snooze key is cleared when the snoozed alarm fires (isSnooze), or by PendingAlerts.clear when the reminder is cancelled (done, deleted or re-scheduled). It is not cleared 'at the next occurrence'. The fire path clears it on any snooze fire. The snooze duration is a global setting (alarmSettings.snoozeMinutes), not per occurrence.

ReminderEntity.repeatIntervalMillis packs two meanings into one column. EVERY_INTERVAL stores a duration in millis and WEEKDAYS stores a day bitmask. RepeatRule.RandomDays also packs minDays*1000+maxDays into the same column. The enum comment mentions only two meanings and omits RandomDays.

RepeatRule has more cases than the plain None/Daily/Weekly/Monthly set: EveryInterval(Duration), Weekdays(Set<DayOfWeek>) and RandomDays(minDays, maxDays). RandomDays is seeded deterministically from the occurrence it follows (RepeatSchedule.stepOnce).

The reminder has no occurrence identity. One row per reminder holds a single dueAt, which is the next occurrence, and the rule rolls it forward in place. There is no per-occurrence key, series id or exception table, so per-occurrence edits have nothing to attach to.

There are two separate merge stamp groups: schedule (scheduleUpdatedAtMillis, scheduleUpdatedByDevice) and status (statusUpdatedAtMillis, statusUpdatedByDevice). The done and notified flags are status, and dueAtIso, the repeat rule and nag settings are schedule. They merge independently through ReminderMerge.

Deletion is a soft-delete tombstone column, deletedAtMillis (Long?), and also done/notified booleans on the row. The row also carries nag columns (nagEnabled, nagMaxRepeats, nagMaxDurationMillis) and soundRef.

RepeatSchedule has skippedOccurrences(firedAt, rule, now), which returns a count of missed occurrences while catching up (capped by MAX_CATCH_UP_STEPS). It is not a user skip action and stores nothing.

The edit UI, ReminderSheet, has a RepeatMode enum and no scope choice such as 'only this' or 'this and following'. Its only 'skip' hit is skipPartiallyExpanded. Editing the sheet rewrites the whole rule and dueAt.
